event: THE definitive carve-out date, in the Fed's own words, current release: table S1M.b's own footnote reads verbatim: 'Sector includes domestic hedge funds (through 2012q3), private equity funds, and personal trusts.' I.e. domestic hedge funds were commingled into the household/nonprofit sector THROUGH 2012:Q3 and are separately identified from 2012:Q4 onward. Independently corroborated, not just quoted: we pulled the actual corporate-equities holder-line data (FU623064105.Q, 'Hedge funds (domestic)') and it is EXACTLY zero every quarter through 2012:Q4 and first non-zero 2013:Q1; the separate hedge-fund-shares instrument (F522.2) shows the identical pattern (first non-zero LEVEL 2012:Q4, first non-zero FLOW 2013:Q1). Three independent readings (a footnote and two raw data series) agree on the same quarter.
source_label: Table S1M.b footnote, current (11 Sep 2026) release
note: CORRECTS an earlier, less precise version of this finding: the carve-out was NOT applied to the entire published history back to 1945 -- pre-2012:Q4 data still has domestic hedge funds fully commingled into the household residual. Every quarter in this project's own 2015:Q1-2026:Q2 window (P1's netbuyers table) falls entirely AFTER the cutover, so none of our headline numbers straddle this discontinuity.

event: Technical Q&A describes the PRE-CARVE-OUT mechanism (and, per the above, this remained the live mechanism for hedge funds when this Q&A was posted -- 2012:Q4 had only just occurred): a DOMESTIC hedge fund's whole portfolio (stocks, bonds, everything) is 'consolidated on the household balance sheet (like nonprofits)' -- indistinguishable from direct household holdings. An OFFSHORE hedge fund is part of 'rest of the world'; a US household buying into it shows up as ROW equity issuance, which flows through the residual calculation into the household purchases line. We found NO later Q&A stating this OFFSHORE pass-through was ever fixed -- unlike the domestic case, it appears to still apply.
source_label: Technical Q&A (undated page, this entry posted 2/26/2014)

event: FEDS Note formalizes that corporate equities excludes mutual fund shares, inter-corporate holdings, treasury stock, and >10%-ownership FDI stakes; states explicitly that 'the household sector holdings are obtained residually by subtracting the holdings of the other sectors from the total value of equities outstanding.'
note: Defines the INSTRUMENT boundary (what counts as 'corporate equities' at all), not a change to who holds it.

event: FEDS Note introduces supplementary ANNUAL tables B.101.h/S14.b (households only) and B.101.n/S15.b (nonprofits only), built by independently estimating nonprofits from IRS Statistics of Income (Form 990/990-PF) then subtracting that from the combined B.101/S1M.b total. States nonprofits are ~6% of combined net worth (2018:Q3). Also states explicitly: because these are residual tables, 'both B.101.h and B.101 will include the assets and liabilities of institutions that are not well captured elsewhere in the Financial Accounts, the most prominent of which are hedge funds and other private equity funds' -- written a year AFTER the 2012:Q3 hedge-fund cutover above, which is a real tension: our best resolution is that this 2019 sentence is about instrument categories OTHER than corporate equities specifically (e.g. debt securities, deposits, alternative assets), where no equivalent carve-out exists -- we did not audit every other instrument line to confirm this.
note: NOT a carve-out of the corporate-equities INSTRUMENT table itself -- the holder line 'Households and nonprofit organizations' in F51.1/L.224 (our $3,069.4bn series) remains a COMBINED household+nonprofit figure. B.101.h/B.101.n is a separate, annual, approximate, residual-of-a-residual presentation of a broader (whole-balance-sheet) concept.

event: Technical Q&A entries PUBLICLY DOCUMENT table B.101.f, 'Balance Sheet of Domestic Hedge Funds', built from Form PF (SEC) data. This is when the Fed explained the methodology to the public -- the data itself had already changed starting 2012:Q4 per the footnote above; this is the documentation catching up, not the cutover date.

Table renumbering Q&A states explicitly: 'tables F.227 and L.227 are skipped; these are reserved for the hedge fund shares instrument to be released at a later date.' I.e. a household's OWNERSHIP STAKE IN a hedge fund (distinct from the hedge fund's own trading, already separated in 2012:Q4) still had no distinct instrument code as of this date -- odd, since our own data shows the underlying series (F522.2 / FU153064705.Q) already existed with real values back to 2012:Q4-2013:Q1. Our best reading: the SERIES existed internally before the TABLE was published.
note: Confirms the hedge-fund-shares LIABILITY-side instrument had no PUBLISHED table as its own instrument as of this date.

event: Current release's own 'Recent Developments' page states plainly: 'Because nonprofit organizations account for a small fraction of the assets and liabilities of the households and nonprofit organizations sector, the sector is commonly referred to as the household sector.' Separately, the SAME page's Table 1 'Corporate equities' line ($74.0 trillion, 2026:Q2) is a BROADER concept than our $3,069.4bn/$52.1trn figures: its footnote states it 'include[s] both directly held securities and securities held indirectly in mutual funds, defined contribution pension plans, and variable life insurance and annuity products.'
note: DENOMINATOR WARNING: the Fed publishes at least THREE different 'household equity' aggregates -- (1) corporate equities ALONE [F51.1/L.224; our $3,069.4bn flow / $52.1trn level headline], (2) corporate equities + mutual fund shares COMBINED [used by DFA and by B.101.h/B.101.n; ~$57.1trn at 2026:Q1], and (3) (1)+(2) plus DC pensions and variable annuities, ALL look-through ['Table 1' in Recent Developments; $74.0trn at 2026:Q2]. Never mix these three without saying which one a number refers to.
